speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand your concern about your infant's bilious vomiting, inability to pass meconium, and abdominal distension; these are critical signs that need immediate investigation. To narrow down the cause, was the baby born via vaginal delivery or cesarean section, and have there been any family members with bowel obstructions or Hirschsprung's disease?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-day-old male infant. The infant was born via a home birth without complications. The mother reports that the infant has had bilious vomiting and has not been able to pass meconium since birth. She also notes that the infant's abdomen appears distended.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Hirschsprung Disease. The clinical presentation of bilious vomiting, failure to pass meconium within 48 hours of a normal vaginal birth, and abdominal distension is highly specific for this condition. I recommend an urgent Abdominal_X-Ray and a Contrast_Enema to confirm the diagnosis and assess for meconium plug syndrome, which can also present similarly.
